subject: goby fish waterfall
title: This Fish Climbs 330-Foot Waterfalls Using Its Mouth

scenes.text: This fish climbs waterfalls. With its mouth.
Hawaii's Nopili rock-climbing goby scales waterfalls as tall as a hundred meters. That's 330 feet.
It climbs with two suckers, and one of them is its mouth.
Stick, pull, stick again. It inches up the wet rock against the falling water.
The same mouth scrapes algae off stones, with almost the same movement. Nobody knows which came first, eating or climbing.
For a human, one scientist said, it's like a marathon. Straight up a cliff.

description:
The Nopili rock-climbing goby of Hawaii climbs waterfalls as tall as 100 metres (330 feet).
It inches upward using two suckers, one of them its mouth, which it also uses to scrape algae off rocks. A 2013 study in PLOS ONE led by Clemson University found the jaw movements for feeding and climbing are very similar, and it is still unclear which evolved first. Scaled to body size, the researchers compared the climb to a human doing a marathon up a vertical cliff against rushing water.
Which animal makes the hardest journey?
first_comment: Adults grow to about seven inches. Would you take the marathon up a cliff, or stay in the ocean?
